gloss: to hang down; to suspend from above

definitions.gloss: to hang down; to suspend from above; to dangle
definitions.explanation: To attach something to a higher point so that it hangs freely. Used for physical objects suspended from ceilings, hooks, branches, and similar supports.

examples.japanese: ランプを{天井|てんじょう}から{吊|つ}り{下|さ}げる。
examples.english: To hang a lamp from the ceiling.

examples.japanese: {首|くび}からカメラを{吊|つ}り{下|さ}げていた。
examples.english: He had a camera hanging from his neck.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{枝|えだ}から{風鈴|ふうりん}を{吊|つ}り{下|さ}げると、{涼|すず}しげな{音|おと}がした。
examples.english: When I hung a wind chime from a tree branch, it made a cool, refreshing sound.

notes:
A compound verb from {吊|つ}る (to hang, to suspend) + {下|さ}げる (to lower). The combination emphasizes that the object is hanging downward from its attachment point.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive. The intransitive counterpart is {吊|つ}り{下|さ}がる (to hang down, to be suspended).
- {吊|つ}り{下|さ}げる — to hang something (transitive)
- {吊|つ}り{下|さ}がる — to be hanging (intransitive)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {天井|てんじょう}から{吊|つ}り{下|さ}げる — to hang from the ceiling
- {首|くび}から{吊|つ}り{下|さ}げる — to hang from one's neck
- {吊|つ}り{下|さ}げ{式|しき} — suspended type, hanging type
- {吊|つ}り{下|さ}げ{広告|こうこく} — hanging advertisement (train ads)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {掛|か}ける — to hang (on a hook or wall; broader usage)
- ぶら{下|さ}げる — to dangle, to hang (more casual; emphasizes swinging)
- {垂|た}らす — to let hang down, to droop (letting something drop loosely)
